nodes.name: Every 15 Minutes
nodes.notes: Matches the interval named in docs/architecture.md section 4. Adjust freely in n8n -- this doesn't need a code change, just edit the trigger node directly.

parameters.query:
select
  r.id as run_id,
  r.tenant_id,
  r.lead_id,
  r.sequence_id,
  r.current_step_index,
  r.created_at as run_created_at,
  s.steps,
  l.contact_id,
  c.name as contact_name,
  c.email as contact_email,
  ac.autonomy_rules,
  ac.connected_gmail_address,
  exists (
    select 1 from messages m
    join conversations conv on conv.id = m.conversation_id
    where conv.contact_id = l.contact_id
      and m.role = 'user'
      and m.created_at > r.created_at
  ) as contact_replied
from follow_up_runs r
join follow_up_sequences s on s.id = r.sequence_id
join leads l on l.id = r.lead_id
join contacts c on c.id = l.contact_id
join ai_config ac on ac.tenant_id = r.tenant_id
where r.status = 'running' and r.next_run_at <= now()
order by r.next_run_at asc
limit 25;

nodes.name: Query Due Runs
nodes.notes: Everything needed per due run in ONE query -- steps, contact info, autonomy_rules, AND the contact_replied check, all as a correlated subquery/join. Deliberately avoids chaining multiple Postgres nodes here: each one would either replace $json with just its RETURNING columns, or (worse) vanish the item entirely if it matched zero rows. One row per due run, capped at 25 per sweep so a backlog can't overload a single execution.

nodes.name: Insert Email Draft
nodes.notes: ALWAYS insert a draft, regardless of autonomy mode -- full audit trail either way, matching the project's core design principle (every AI decision logged). status is 'auto_sent' or 'pending' depending on mode (set upstream in Determine Action). The 'pending' case surfaces in the dashboard's existing Pending Approvals screen for free -- no new UI needed.

nodes.name: Send via Gmail
nodes.notes: Same known limitation as everywhere else in this codebase: one shared Gmail credential per workflow, not dynamic per-tenant. Whichever tenant's inbox this credential belongs to is the only one that can actually autonomous-send today. continueOnFail:true -- the draft row is already saved, so a send failure never loses the record, and the run still advances below regardless (see Advance Run's note on this tradeoff).

parameters.query:
update follow_up_runs r
set current_step_index = current_step_index + 1,
    status = case when $2 then 'completed' else 'running' end,
    next_run_at = case when $2 then null else r.created_at + ($3 || ' days')::interval end,
    updated_at = now()
from (select id from follow_up_runs where id = $1) sub
where r.id = sub.id;

nodes.name: Advance Run
nodes.notes: KNOWN, DELIBERATE LIMITATION: this runs immediately after queuing the draft, regardless of whether an approval_required draft has actually been approved and sent yet by a human. If approvals lag, the sequence keeps advancing to the next scheduled step on time anyway rather than waiting -- drafts can pile up in the approvals queue while the schedule marches forward. Documented here and in the spec doc, not hidden. Fixing it properly would mean tying advancement to 15 (Send Approved Email) confirming an actual send, which would require editing an already-live production workflow -- deliberately out of scope for this version.
